words.definition: A small rocky object that orbits the Sun, mostly found in the region between Mars and Jupiter.

contextSentences.en: The asteroid 2004 BL86 flew past Earth at a distance of about 1.2 million kilometres.
Scientists study the composition of asteroids to learn about the early solar system.

words.example_en: During the night observation, the telescope tracked an asteroid moving slowly across the background stars.
words.example_sk: Počas nočného pozorovania teleskop sledoval asteroid, ktorý sa pomaly pohyboval cez hviezdne pozadie.

words.definition: The layer of gases surrounding a planet, moon, or other celestial body.

contextSentences.en: The Earth's atmosphere is divided into several layers, including the troposphere and stratosphere.
Without a protective atmosphere, the surface of a planet is exposed to harmful radiation.

words.example_en: As the probe descended through Titan's atmosphere, its instruments recorded unexpected changes in temperature and pressure.
words.example_sk: Keď sonda klesala cez atmosféru Titanu, jej prístroje zaznamenali neočakávané zmeny teploty a tlaku.

words.definition: A region in space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from it.

contextSentences.en: The first ever image of a black hole was captured and released in 2019.
Nothing, not even light, can escape the gravitational pull of a black hole.

words.example_en: By tracking the rapid motion of nearby stars, astronomers gathered strong evidence for a black hole at the center of the galaxy.
words.example_sk: Sledovaním rýchleho pohybu blízkych hviezd získali astronómovia silné dôkazy o čiernej diere v strede galaxie.

words.definition: A small icy body in space that orbits the sun and develops a bright tail when it passes close to it.

contextSentences.en: Halley's comet is visible from Earth roughly every 75 years.
As the comet approached the Sun, it developed a bright, glowing tail.

words.example_en: As the comet approached the Sun, astronomers tracked the growth of its tail with telescopes around the world.
words.example_sk: Keď sa kométa priblížila k Slnku, astronómovia sledovali rast jej chvosta pomocou teleskopov po celom svete.

words.definition: A group of stars forming a recognizable pattern in the night sky.

contextSentences.en: The constellation Orion is one of the easiest to spot in the winter night sky.
Ancient sailors used the positions of constellations to navigate at sea.

words.example_en: As the sky grew darker, the guide pointed out the constellation Orion above the observatory dome.
words.example_sk: Keď obloha tmavla, sprievodca ukázal na súhvezdie Orion nad kupolou observatória.

words.definition: An event in which one celestial body moves into the shadow of another or blocks its light.

contextSentences.en: During a total solar eclipse, the Moon completely blocks the Sun's light.
A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon.

words.example_en: We gathered to watch the solar eclipse in the sky at the moment of totality.
words.example_sk: Zišli sme sa, aby sme mohli sledovať zatmenie slnka v okamihu najväčšieho zatmenia.

words.definition: A vast system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter held together by gravity.

contextSentences.en: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, contains an estimated 200 to 400 billion stars.
The Andromeda galaxy is the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way.

words.example_en: Using infrared data, the team mapped the outer arms of the galaxy and found regions where new stars are forming.
words.example_sk: Pomocou infračervených údajov tím zmapoval vonkajšie ramená galaxie a našiel oblasti, kde vznikajú nové hviezdy.

words.definition: The force that attracts objects toward each other, especially toward the Earth or other large bodies in space.

contextSentences.en: Gravity keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun and the Moon around the Earth.
Albert Einstein described gravity as a curvature of space and time.

words.example_en: Without gravity, the gas and dust in the nebula would never collapse to form new stars.
words.example_sk: Bez gravitácie by sa plyn a prach v hmlovine nikdy nezrútili a nevytvorili nové hviezdy.

words.definition: Relating to the Moon.

contextSentences.en: The lunar surface is covered with craters formed by meteorite impacts.
The lunar cycle lasts approximately 29.5 days and influences ocean tides.

words.example_en: During the eclipse, the observatory streamed close-up images of the lunar surface to schools around the country.
words.example_sk: Počas zatmenia hvezdáreň vysielala detailné zábery mesačného povrchu do škôl po celej krajine.

words.definition: A streak of light produced when a small object from space enters the Earth's atmosphere and burns up.

contextSentences.en: During the Perseid meteor shower, hundreds of meteors can be seen in a single night.
A meteor burns up as it enters the Earth's atmosphere, creating a streak of light.

words.example_en: During the meteor shower, we saw a bright meteor flash across the eastern sky just before dawn.
words.example_sk: Počas meteorického roja sme videli jasný meteor, ktorý krátko pred svitaním preletel cez východnú oblohu.

words.definition: A large cloud of gas and dust in space, often where stars are formed or where the remains of dead stars are found.

contextSentences.en: The Orion Nebula is a region of active star formation visible to the naked eye.
Nebulae are vast clouds of gas and dust that serve as the birthplaces of new stars.

words.example_en: Through the telescope, we could see the nebula glowing faintly around the young star cluster.
words.example_sk: Cez ďalekohľad sme videli, ako hmlovina slabo žiari okolo mladej hviezdokopy.

words.definition: The curved path of an object moving around a star, planet, or other body in space; to move around such a body along that path.

contextSentences.en: The International Space Station completes one orbit of the Earth every 90 minutes.
The Moon travels in a slightly elliptical orbit around the Earth.

words.example_en: The telescope tracked the satellite as it completed another orbit around Earth before dawn.
words.example_sk: Teleskop sledoval satelit, keď pred svitaním dokončil ďalší obeh okolo Zeme.

words.definition: A large round object in space that moves around a star and does not produce its own light.

contextSentences.en: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with a mass greater than all others combined.
Since 2006, Pluto has been classified as a dwarf planet rather than a full planet.

words.example_en: Through the telescope, we could clearly see the planet rising above the horizon just after sunset.
words.example_sk: Cez ďalekohľad sme mohli jasne vidieť planétu, ako sa dvíha nad obzor tesne po západe slnka.

words.definition: The Sun and all the objects that orbit it, including planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.

contextSentences.en: Our solar system formed roughly 4.6 billion years ago from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft has left the solar system and is now travelling through interstellar space.

words.example_en: By comparing distant planetary systems with our solar system, astronomers can better understand how planets form.
words.example_sk: Porovnávaním vzdialených planetárnych systémov s našou slnečnou sústavou môžu astronómovia lepšie pochopiť, ako vznikajú planéty.

words.definition: An instrument used to observe distant objects in space by collecting and focusing light or other forms of radiation.

contextSentences.en: Galileo Galilei was among the first to use a telescope for astronomical observations.
The James Webb Space Telescope provides the most detailed images of the early universe ever taken.

words.example_en: After sunset, we set up the telescope on the hill to watch Jupiter and its moons come into view.
words.example_sk: Po západe slnka sme na kopci postavili ďalekohľad, aby sme sledovali Jupiter a jeho mesiace, ako sa objavujú na oblohe.

words.definition: Relating to the sky, outer space, or the objects in it.
words.example_en: Through the telescope, we tracked several celestial objects moving slowly across the winter sky.
words.example_sk: Cez teleskop sme sledovali niekoľko nebeských objektov, ktoré sa pomaly pohybovali po zimnej oblohe.

words.definition: A large bowl-shaped hole in the ground or on the surface of a planet or moon, often formed by an impact or volcanic activity.
words.example_en: Through the telescope, we could clearly see the shadow along the edge of the lunar crater just after sunset on the Moon.
words.example_sk: Cez ďalekohľad sme tesne po západe Slnka na Mesiaci jasne videli tieň pozdĺž okraja mesačného krátera.

words.definition: An imaginary line around the middle of a planet or other celestial body, equally distant from its poles.
words.example_en: As the spacecraft passed above Jupiter's equator, the team captured detailed images of the planet's fastest-moving cloud bands.
words.example_sk: Keď kozmická loď prelietala nad rovníkom Jupitera, tím zachytil podrobné snímky najrýchlejšie sa pohybujúcich pásov oblakov planéty.

words.definition: Relating to the space between stars.
words.example_en: The probe was designed to survive the harsh conditions of interstellar space after leaving the Solar System.
words.example_sk: Sonda bola navrhnutá tak, aby prežila drsné podmienky medzihviezdneho priestoru po opustení Slnečnej sústavy.

words.definition: An object that moves around a planet or star; it can be natural, like a moon, or artificial, like a spacecraft.
words.example_en: The satellite transmitted detailed images of Jupiter’s storms back to Earth during the mission.
words.example_sk: Satelit počas misie prenášal na Zem podrobné snímky búrok na Jupiteri.

words.definition: The range of different wavelengths or frequencies of electromagnetic radiation, often seen when light is separated into its component colors.
words.example_en: By analyzing the spectrum of the distant star, astronomers identified traces of hydrogen and helium in its outer layers.
words.example_sk: Analýzou spektra vzdialenej hviezdy astronómovia identifikovali stopy vodíka a hélia v jej vonkajších vrstvách.

words.definition: A spacecraft designed for travel between stars or for long-distance journeys in space.
words.example_en: In the novel, the starship adjusted its course to avoid a dense field of asteroids near the outer system.
words.example_sk: V románe kozmická loď upravila svoj kurz, aby sa vyhla hustému poľu asteroidov pri okraji sústavy.

words.definition: All space, time, matter, and energy, including all stars, planets, galaxies, and other forms of cosmic structure.
words.example_en: By studying the faint glow left after the Big Bang, astronomers can learn how the universe changed over billions of years.
words.example_sk: Skúmaním slabého žiarenia, ktoré zostalo po Veľkom tresku, môžu astronómovia zistiť, ako sa vesmír menil počas miliárd rokov.

words.definition: The point in the sky directly above an observer; the highest point or culmination.
words.example_en: At noon the sun reached its zenith.
words.example_sk: Na poludnie poludní slnko dosiahlo svoj zenit.

words.definition: Either of the two times each year when the sun crosses the celestial equator and day and night are approximately equal in length.
words.example_en: The spring equinox marks the beginning of astronomical spring.
words.example_sk: Jarná rovnodennosť označuje začiatok astronomického jara.

words.definition: Either of the two times in the year when the sun is at its greatest distance from the celestial equator, causing the longest day (summer solstice) or the shortest day (winter solstice).
words.example_en: During the winter solstice, the observatory stayed open all night so visitors could track Orion rising over the snowy horizon.
words.example_sk: Počas zimného slnovratu zostalo observatórium otvorené celú noc, aby návštevníci mohli sledovať, ako Orion vychádza nad zasneženým obzorom.

words.definition: A unit of distance equal to how far light travels in one year, used to measure vast distances in space.
words.example_en: The telescope revealed a galaxy more than ten million light-years away, yet its glow was still visible on a clear night.
words.example_sk: Teleskop odhalil galaxiu vzdialenú viac ako desať miliónov svetelných rokov, no jej žiara bola za jasnej noci stále viditeľná.

words.definition: A powerful explosion of a star that suddenly becomes extremely bright and releases a vast amount of energy.
words.example_en: Astronomers monitored the supernova for weeks, tracking how its brightness changed after the explosion.
words.example_sk: Astronómovia sledovali supernovu celé týždne a zaznamenávali, ako sa jej jas po výbuchu menil.

words.definition: The path that an object follows through space as it moves, especially under the influence of gravity or other forces.
words.example_en: By adjusting the spacecraft’s trajectory, mission controllers ensured it would pass close enough to Mars to capture detailed images.
words.example_sk: Úpravou trajektórie kozmickej lode riadiace stredisko misie zabezpečilo, že preletí dostatočne blízko pri Marse, aby zachytila podrobné snímky.

words.definition: The movement of an object turning around its own axis.
words.example_en: By measuring the Sun's rotation, astronomers can track how magnetic activity changes across its surface.
words.example_sk: Meraním rotácie Slnka môžu astronómovia sledovať, ako sa na jeho povrchu mení magnetická aktivita.
